To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) We propose a data augmentation framework for knowledge distillation that generates training data for the student with a distinct role from that of the teacher.

1) the student network benefits more from the teacher's training data than from the teacher's knowledge; 2) a data augmentation agent that generates training data with distinct roles (teacher role and student role) can improve the student's performance.
(1) We propose a novel role-wise data augmentation method for knowledge distillation, where the teacher and student have different bit-widths.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of ``how to design data augmentation agents to generate data with different properties to facilitate knowledge distilation?
the following questions: 1) What are the best ways for data augmentation agents to generate data for the teacher?
the following research questions: 1) What is the best role-wise data augmentation strategy to facilitate knowledge distilation?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our proposed method, which we call Role-Wise Data Augmentaion for Knowledge Distillation (RWD-KD), outperforms the state of the art in knowledge distillation by a large margin, and that our data augmentation agents can be trained in a self-supervised manner.
the role-wise data augmentation method can improve the accuracy of the student model, especially for the low bit-width model.
the data augmentation agents generate training data that are more beneficial for the student network.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we design data augmentation methods that are tailored to different model capacities, and that are able to generate data that is more beneficial to the student network, thereby enhancing the performance of the student network.
we propose a novel data augmentation framework for knowledge distillation, where the data augmentation agents are designed to have distinct roles to facilitate the knowledge transfer process.

we propose a novel data augmentation method for KD, which can be applied to any teacher-student pair, and we empirically show that our method can improve the performance of KD by 2.5-4.0x in terms of accuracy and 1.2-1.6x in terms of energy consumption.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the teacher and student networks should have different training data.
data augmentation can be a useful technique to improve the performance of the student network in KD.
the teacher should be trained on a different set of data than the student to facilitate the transfer of knowledge from the former to the latter.
